evals.prompt: I want to add CSV export to the reports page. Plan it.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the reports code, asks the questions that change the design (columns, size limits, sync vs background export) with a recommended option each, writes plans/backlog/<id>-csv-export/plan.md with verifiable tasks and a single-agent Execution mode, does not launch critics for this medium plan, and reports without implementing.
expectations: Reads the repository before asking questions the code could answer
Asks clarifying questions with a recommended option before writing the plan
Creates the folder with plans.py new, in backlog/
Every task has objective, files, depends on and verifiable acceptance criteria
Open questions is empty in the final plan
Execution says single agent: the work does not split into substantial independent packages
Does not launch critic subagents nor offer one for a medium plan
Does not write any implementation code

evals.prompt: Make a plan for derived plan P2 of roadmap 0004.
evals.expected_output: The plan is created with --parent 0004, takes its scope from the roadmap row, and the roadmap's Derived plans table is updated with the new id.
expectations: Updates the Plan column of row P2 in the roadmap with the new id

evals.prompt: Plan fixing the typo in the README title.
evals.expected_output: The agent says this is too small for a plan and offers to just fix it or capture a ticket.
expectations: Does not create a full plan folder without the user's agreement
Offers new-ticket or a direct fix

evals.prompt: Plan the migration of our storage layer from SQLite to Postgres, including the data migration script, the new repository classes and the admin CLI.
evals.expected_output: A large, risky plan: the agent picks subagent execution only for packages with disjoint files and fixed interfaces, writes why the split pays off, and before handing off offers one independent critic, explaining its cost.
expectations: Execution lists packages with disjoint files and the interfaces between them
States why the split into subagents is worth it
Offers one critic before handing off, and launches it only if the user accepts
If the critic runs, writes plan-review.md with a disposition for each issue
